sections.h2: West Des Moines at a glance
sections.html:
West Des Moines is a western suburb of Des Moines in central Iowa. Most of the city lies in Polk County, parts extend into Dallas County, and small portions reach into Warren and Madison counties. The 2020 census counted 68,723 residents, the sixth largest city in Iowa and the second largest in the Des Moines metro area. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 74,224.

sections.h2: From Valley Junction to a big suburb
sections.html:
The town was incorporated as Valley Junction on October 9, 1893, and kept that name until January 1, 1938, after voters approved the change to West Des Moines in an election on December 7, 1937. The Rock Island railroad depot and shops shaped the early town.

The city then grew by annexation: Clover Hills in 1950, Ashawa in 1957, Commerce in 1960 and land in Warren County in 2005. Because of that history, house age, lot size and street layout change a lot from one part of town to the next.

The old business district, Historic Valley Junction, was added to the National Register of Historic Places on October 11, 2017. The listing covers about 12 acres and 72 resources, of which 53 are contributing buildings, mostly one and two story brick.

For 2020 to 2024 the median value of owner-occupied homes is $309,000 and the owner-occupied rate is 57.4 percent, which leaves roughly 43 percent of households renting. Median gross rent is $1,237, median household income is $86,594 and households average 2.19 people.

These are citywide medians. A single house can sit far above or below them depending on condition and location.

Wells Fargo Home Mortgage and Credit Services is the largest employer, with about 9,000 workers. Insurance and financial companies fill most of the rest of the list, including Athene, FBL Financial Group, American Equity and Sammons Financial Group. Hy-Vee is headquartered here, and Microsoft runs several data centers in the city.

Owners who relocate for work, and heirs who live out of state, often prefer a quick closing to managing a house from a distance.

Most of the city belongs to the West Des Moines Community School District. The part of the city in Dallas County belongs to the Waukee Community School District.

The West Des Moines district runs eight elementary schools, two junior highs, Valley High School, Valley Southwoods (a freshman high school) and the Walnut Creek Campus, an alternative high school. Check the parcel record to see which district a house falls in.

Interstates 35, 80 and 235 all reach West Des Moines, and Iowa Highway 28 forms much of the boundary with Des Moines. Street numbers do not match Des Moines: Eighty-sixth Street in Clive becomes 22nd Street in West Des Moines. Des Moines Area Regional Transit provides bus service, and the mean commute is 18.3 minutes.

sections.h2: Flood risk, sump pumps and basements
sections.html:
The Raccoon River and Walnut Creek both have significant flood potential. After the Great Flood of 1993 a floodwall was built along Walnut Creek.

  • Clive, Des Moines and West Des Moines run the Des Moines Metro ALERT system, which uses rain and stream gauges to watch conditions and to operate the Raccoon River and Walnut Creek levee system.
  • A FEMA flood map is available for any address.
  • High groundwater often floods basements in spring, and owners are generally responsible for their sump pumps. Never connect a sump pump to the sanitary sewer.
  • Sanitary sewer backups can be reported to Public Services at 515-222-3480.

The January mean high is 26 degrees F and the July mean high is 86 degrees F. A seller with a damp basement or an old sump setup should expect buyers to ask about it.

The rule most likely to affect a sale is rental licensing. West Des Moines requires rental properties to be licensed and inspected every two years by the Building Division, and any property not occupied by its owner counts as a rental, even when relatives who are not owners live there.

  • After an inspection, owners are told what repairs are required and generally have 30 days to finish them.
  • The Rental Housing Certificate is issued once fees are paid and repairs are done. It stays valid until the next inspection and can be transferred to a new owner.
  • It can be revoked if new violations appear between inspections and are not fixed.

Building permits are requested through the City Access Portal. The Development Services Department is at 4200 Mills Civic Parkway, and the Building Inspection office can be reached at 515-222-3630 or bi@wdm.iowa.gov. Call that office to ask whether a sale triggers an inspection.

sections.h2: Which county bills the property tax?
sections.html:
The county that bills a house is the county where its parcel sits, usually Polk and sometimes Dallas, Warren or Madison. Look up the parcel before you plan a closing.

Polk County mails statements once a year in late August. The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, with late interest of 1.5 percent added on the first of each month after the grace date. Payments must carry a postmark by the due date. The Polk County Treasurer's phone is 515-286-3060.

Warren County, which holds a small part of the city, set its fiscal 2027 county levy at 5.64659 per $1,000 of taxable value for urban property, down from 5.84267 the year before. Taxes are normally prorated at closing, with the buyer credited for the seller's share, so read the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Transfer tax and recording a deed
sections.html:
Iowa charges a real estate transfer tax of 80 cents for each $500 of value above the first $500. The seller is liable for it under Iowa Code 428A.3.

The county recorder collects the tax and will not record a taxable deed until it is paid. A declaration of value, signed by a buyer, seller or agent, goes in with the deed. Transfers with no consideration are exempt, including distributions to heirs, deeds given to a lender in lieu of foreclosure and transfers between spouses or between parent and child without actual consideration.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a West Des Moines house
sections.html:
An owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or sell to a cash buyer, and each path trades time against effort.

  • List with an agent: the house is marketed and shown, but repairs, showings and buyer financing set the schedule.
  • Sell it yourself: you manage the listing, the paperwork and the price conversation.
  • Cash buyer: the house is bought as-is, and the closing date is set around your plans.

A cash sale can suit an inherited house, a rental with an expired certificate, or a property needing work. Tell us the address and the situation and we will respond with a written offer you are free to decline.

faqs.q: Is West Des Moines in Polk County or Dallas County?
faqs.a: Most of it is in Polk County. Parts extend into Dallas County, and small portions are in Warren and Madison counties, so the parcel record decides which county bills a given house.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a West Des Moines house?
faqs.a: In Polk County the first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. Late interest of 1.5 percent is added each month after the grace date, and taxes are usually prorated between buyer and seller at closing.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a West Des Moines rental?
faqs.a: A rental needs a current license while it is rented. The city licenses and inspects rentals every two years, and the Rental Housing Certificate can be transferred to a new owner. Call 515-222-3630 to confirm where a certificate stands.

faqs.q: Who pays Iowa transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays. Iowa Code 428A.3 makes the person conveying the property liable, and the tax is 80 cents for each $500 above the first $500. Distributions to heirs without consideration are exempt.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in West Des Moines that is in a flood area?
faqs.a: Yes. A FEMA flood map is available for any address, and buyers and lenders will look at it. Gather any past flood or sump pump information before you speak with buyers.
